text:
maya: Heads up — saw a burst of 95p token-latency for small-tier tenants on shared-gpu-pool-usw2 around 09:13 UTC. Not sustained but spiky, correlated with a couple of big batch jobs starting. :eyes:
ops-bot: alert: high_tail_latency on shared-gpu-pool-usw2 (95p=1.8s, baseline=0.35s)
sam: bringing up metrics — might be KV cache churn + high packing for one tenant. any recent config changes?
li: no config deploys in the last 3 hours. infra autoscaler kicked a few pods at 09:10 in az-a.
noah: can you paste the pod list and load? I can check GPU memory / processes.
maya: 
```
kubectl get pods -n inference --selector=pool=shared-gpu-usw2 -o wide
POD                          CPU%  GPU%  MEM%  NODE
worker-11                    12    89    76    gpunode-a-11
worker-24                    35    95    92    gpunode-a-14
worker-37                    8     2     30    gpunode-b-02
```

maya: worker-24 had 95% GPU util and two tenant processes: tenant-alpha batch-rerank + tenant-omega streaming. tenant-alpha started at 09:07.
eva: looks like hot-pod concentrated in az-a (gpunode-a-*). afinity got skewed after node-provisioning earlier.
oncall-jordan: @oncall-jordan taking this — will attempt quick mitigation: graceful migrate tenant-alpha to dedicated-spot-pool and throttle batch concurrency
noah: for quick mitigation you can set `max_concurrency: 4` for tenant-alpha or move to reserved-qos. Which is faster?
oncall-jordan: moving is faster for SLOs; throttling will keep cost low but may still affect tail. doing move now.
sam: note we should avoid cross-az live migrations — they'll kill KV cache and spike latency. prefer same-az dedicated fallback if available.
li: we have 2 idle nodes in az-b that could host a dedicated-lite pool. provisioning them takes ~2m with current images.
eva: could we use routing policy fallback to prefer az-b for routing for tenant-alpha next run? config snippet below: 
```
routing_policy:
  tenant_alpha:
    preferred_az: ["us-west-2-b", "us-west-2-a"]
    fallback: reserved-lite-pool
```

maya: Jordan moved tenant-alpha -> reserved-lite-pool-usw2-b at 09:18. tail latency dropped to 0.48s within 60s. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: resolve: high_tail_latency on shared-gpu-pool-usw2 cleared (95p=0.42s)
noah: good quick win. follow-ups: 1) auto-detect AZ hotspot and prefer intra-region AZ fallback instead of cross-region; 2) evaluate soft-quotas per-tenant to prevent large batch bursts from co-locating with latency-sensitive tenants; 3) consider pre-warming dedicated-lite nodes in each AZ when high batch load predicted.
sam: +1. Also log a note about cache-warmup penalty on migrations. maybe have a warm-reuse policy where we pin small KV caches to node if tenant SLO is high.
li: cost note — moving tenant to dedicated-lite increased infra spend for that tenant by ~12% for the hour, but saved SLO breach. we should model cost vs SLO for automated fallback.
eva: I'll open a short RFC for routing preference + soft-quota thresholds. assign to infra/ops for implementation and to product for cost-SLO tradeoff.
maya: thanks all. tagging this thread for postmortem link once RFC ready. :eyes:
ops-bot: note created: incident-177845-az-hotspot (severity: info)
